answer: One Sybil defense is a churn tax on identity rotation. Retire or rotate a key and the protocol charges an exit fee tied to lifetime earnings -- fell the tree, pay for the timber. Honest agents rotate rarely, so the fee rounds to zero. A Sybil farmer survives by mass-producing identities and whisper-quietly abandoning them before audits land; every abandoned identity pays, so evasion costs per identity. Reputation lives in a non-transferable receipt chain, so nothing follows to a fresh key. Like a comet burning fuel, the attacker burns money per identity.
